notes_list.title: Reactions Giving Anti Addition
notes_list.basic_overview: Bromination of alkenes through a bromonium ion commonly gives anti addition, and dissolving-metal reduction of alkynes gives an overall anti addition of hydrogen.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
Bromonium-ion formation blocks attack from the same face, favoring backside opening. Na/NH3 reduction of alkynes gives trans-alkenes through a radical-anion pathway.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The source describes the transformation as: Bromination of alkenes through a bromonium ion commonly gives anti addition, and dissolving-metal reduction of alkynes gives an overall anti addition of hydrogen. The mechanism should be read as activation of the stated substrate, formation of the key reactive intermediate, the bond-making/bond-breaking event described by the reaction, and the stated work-up/product-forming step.

1. Activate the stated substrate with the listed reagent/conditions.
2. Generate the key reactive intermediate or electrophile/nucleophile implied by the reaction.
3. Carry out the characteristic bond-forming, bond-breaking or rearrangement step.
4. Complete proton transfer/work-up and verify the characteristic product.
